title: 10 Lectures and 42 Open Problems — The Paley ETF Conjecture
exact_target: Does the Paley frame preserve sparse-vector norms for sparsity growing faster than the square root of its size?
definition_tex:
\subsection{Definitions and mathematical statement}
Let $p\equiv1\pmod4$ be prime and let $Q\subset\mathbb F_p^*$ be
the nonzero quadratic residues. Form a matrix $A_p$ with rows
$\{0\}\cup Q$ and columns $\mathbb F_p\cup\{\infty\}$ by
\[
 (A_p)_{0j}=p^{-1/2},\quad
 (A_p)_{rj}=(2/p)^{1/2}e^{2\pi i rj/p}\quad(r\in Q,j\in\mathbb F_p),
 \qquad (A_p)_{\cdot,\infty}=e_0.
\]
The vector $e_0$ is one in row zero and zero elsewhere. This is the
unit-column-norm Paley equiangular tight frame, of size
$(p+1)/2$ by $p+1$. Distinct columns have inner-product magnitude
$p^{-1/2}$.

For $s\ge1$, set
\[
 \delta_s(A_p)=\max_{|J|\le s}
                 \|(A_p)_J^*(A_p)_J-I_{|J|}\|_{\mathrm{op}},
\]
where $J$ is a column subset and the norm is the largest singular
value. Does there exist a fixed $\delta<1$ and an integer function
$s(p)$ with $s(p)/\sqrt p\to\infty$ such that
$\delta_{s(p)}(A_p)\le\delta$ for all sufficiently large such primes?

Even an unbounded logarithmic improvement over $\sqrt p$ is sought;
a fixed constant multiple of $\sqrt p$ does not suffice. Equivalently,
all coefficient vectors on each permissible column set must have their
squared norm preserved within factors $1\pm\delta$. The question is
unconditional for this specific arithmetic frame, not a random choice
of Fourier rows or a conclusion assuming an unproved distribution
property of quadratic residues.

\subsection{Short English statement}
Does the Paley frame preserve sparse-vector norms for sparsity growing faster than the square root of its size?

\subsection{Sources}
\begin{itemize}
\item[S1] ULAM.AI and the UnsolvedMath Contributors, supplied problems.json, record 2800604 (AMR-027-0604), AMR Open Problem Lists. Catalogue identity and source transcription; CC BY 4.0.
\url{https://huggingface.co/datasets/ulamai/UnsolvedMath}.
\item[S2] Bandeira - 42 Open Problems in Data Science (2016), Open Problem 6.4. Original source indexed by AMR-027-0604.
\url{https://afonsobandeira.wordpress.com/2015/12/07/10l42pcompressedsensing/}.
\item[S3] A. S. Bandeira, Ten Lectures and Forty-Two Open Problems in the Mathematics of Data Science, corresponding numbered problem and surrounding definitions.
\url{https://people.math.ethz.ch/~abandeira/TenLecturesFortyTwoProblems.pdf}.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Definitions and mathematical statement}
Let $p\equiv1\pmod4$ be prime and let $Q\subset\mathbb F_p^*$ be
the nonzero quadratic residues. Form a matrix $A_p$ with rows
$\{0\}\cup Q$ and columns $\mathbb F_p\cup\{\infty\}$ by

unit-column-norm Paley equiangular tight frame, of size
$(p+1)/2$ by $p+1$. Distinct columns have inner-product magnitude
$p^{-1/2}$.

\[

                 \|(A_p)_J^*(A_p)_J-I_{|J|}\|_{\mathrm{op}},
\]
where $J$ is a column subset and the norm is the largest singular
value. Does there exist a fixed $\delta<1$ and an integer function
$s(p)$ with $s(p)/\sqrt p\to\infty$ such that
$\delta_{s(p)}(A_p)\le\delta$ for all sufficiently large such primes?

a fixed constant multiple of $\sqrt p$ does not suffice. Equivalently,

property of quadratic residues.

\subsection{Short English statement}
Does the Paley frame preserve sparse-vector norms for sparsity growing faster than the square root of its size?

\subsection{Sources}
\begin{itemize}
\item[S1] ULAM.AI and the UnsolvedMath Contributors, supplied problems.json, record 2800604 (AMR-027-0604), AMR Open Problem Lists. Catalogue identity and source transcription; CC BY 4.0.
\url{https://huggingface.co/datasets/ulamai/UnsolvedMath}.
\item[S2] Bandeira - 42 Open Problems in Data Science (2016), Open Problem 6.4. Original source indexed by AMR-027-0604.
\url{https://afonsobandeira.wordpress.com/2015/12/07/10l42pcompressedsensing/}.
\item[S3] A. S. Bandeira, Ten Lectures and Forty-Two Open Problems in the Mathematics of Data Science, corresponding numbered problem and surrounding definitions.
\url{https://people.math.ethz.ch/~abandeira/TenLecturesFortyTwoProblems.pdf}.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Verbatim supplied catalogue question}
Does the Paley Equiangular tight frame satisfy the Restricted Isometry Property pass the square root bottleneck? (even by logarithmic factors?).

\section{Attempt and results}
Let $p\equiv1\pmod4$ be prime and keep the frame in the original definition.
Write $\chi$ for the quadratic character with $\chi(0)=0$, and
$e_p(t)=e^{2\pi it/p}$. We derive its Gram entries directly, avoiding a
dependence on the sign convention for the quadratic Gauss sum.

\paragraph{Character-sum calculation.}
Set $G=\sum_{t\ne0}\chi(t)e_p(t)$. Half the nonzero field elements are
squares: the map $x\mapsto x^2$ has exactly two preimages for every nonzero
square. Thus $\sum_{t\ne0}\chi(t)=0$. Since $\chi(-1)=1$,
complex conjugation followed by $t\mapsto-t$ shows $G$ is real.
Moreover, put $x=uy$ in the double sum to obtain
\[
|G|^2=\sum_{u\ne0}\chi(u)\sum_{y\ne0}e_p((u-1)y)
=(p-1)-\sum_{u\ne0,1}\chi(u)=p.
\]
Here the inner sum equals $p-1$ at $u=1$ and $-1$ otherwise, by the finite
geometric series. Hence $G=\varepsilon\sqrt p$ for some
$\varepsilon\in\{-1,1\}$; its sign is unnecessary below.
For $i\ne j$ in $\mathbb F_p$, the given row weights give
\[
\langle a_i,a_j\rangle
=\frac1p\left(1+2\sum_{r\in Q}e_p(r(j-i))\right)
=\frac{\chi(j-i)G}{p}.
\]
Indeed $2\boldsymbol1_Q(r)=1+\chi(r)$ for $r\ne0$, the nontrivial
additive-character sum over the whole field is zero, and scaling its argument
multiplies the character sum by $\chi(j-i)$. The infinity column has inner
product $1/\sqrt p$ with every finite column. All columns have norm one.

\paragraph{Exact error on a clique.}
If $J\subset\mathbb F_p$ is a Paley clique of size $q\ge2$, every off-diagonal
character in its Gram matrix is one. Thus its Gram error equals
$\varepsilon(J_q-I_q)/\sqrt p$ and has norm $(q-1)/\sqrt p$.
The same conclusion holds for an independent set, with the sign reversed.
In particular, if $\delta_s(A_p)\le\delta<1$ and
$s>1+\delta\sqrt p$, there cannot be a clique of size exceeding
$1+\delta\sqrt p$: a larger clique has a subset of size
$\lfloor1+\delta\sqrt p\rfloor+1\le s$, contradicting that bound.
This necessary condition does not prove RIP, even if all cliques are small;
arbitrary supports with mixed signs and arbitrary complex coefficients remain.

\paragraph{The attempted absolute-value argument.}
For every support of size $t\le s$, the preceding Gram entries and
$(\sum|x_i|)^2\le t\sum|x_i|^2$ imply
$|\|Ax\|^2-\|x\|^2|\le(t-1)\|x\|^2/\sqrt p$.
Consequently $\delta_s\le(s-1)/\sqrt p$ is a sound elementary bound.
But as $s/\sqrt p\to\infty$ it cannot supply any fixed distortion below one.
The clique computation shows why replacing every sign by a favorable
cancellation assumption is unjustified: some supports have perfectly aligned
signs. It does not show that sufficiently large such supports exist.

\section{Context, audit, and remaining scope}
The original Paley-frame question and its relationship to clique questions
were checked in Bandeira's primary notes on 11 October 2026.
These are elementary standard Gram calculations, not a new cancellation
bound. The audit checked $q=1$ separately (error zero), the infinity column,
Gauss-sum sign independence, and the all-support/all-coefficient quantifiers.
No numerical computation or theorem prover was used in this record.
No unconditional estimate for $s/\sqrt p\to\infty$ was established, and no
unproved character-pseudorandomness hypothesis has been substituted for it.
